tagline: Franklin Roosevelt's parkway, laid out for the views.
intro: From the Thruway connector by Chatham the Taconic runs south 104 miles to Kensico Circle, first along the ridges between the Hudson Valley and the Taconic Mountains, through farms and woods with glimpses west to the Catskills. In Putnam County it narrows and climbs through the Hudson Highlands to its high point, almost 1,200 feet, then widens into a commuter road through Westchester.

Franklin Roosevelt proposed it in 1925 and the last piece opened in 1963. Gilmore Clarke set the long views to open on downgrades and long curves, where they distract least, and faced the overpasses in native stone. Lewis Mumford, no friend of superhighways, told friends coming to see him to take it.

moments.title: Catskill overlooks near Philmont
moments.text: Past a rise beyond the Philmont exit, overlook parking areas on both sides of the road look west across the valley to the Catskills.

moments.title: Clarence Fahnestock State Park
moments.text: For five and a half miles the road crosses the park with no development in sight, climbing past cliffs and rocky outcrops between two lakes to its highest point.

moments.title: New Croton Reservoir
moments.text: In Yorktown the two roadways spread 1,500 feet apart, with houses between them, and cross the reservoir on separate bridges, the northbound one curved to echo the hills.

practical: As on other New York parkways, only passenger vehicles are allowed.
